label: PROMPT: carbamazepine with a macrolide
title: Carbamazepine supplied with clarithromycin or erythromycin
statement: Carbamazepine should not be used in combination with clarithromycin or erythromycin.

source.document: Cooper JA, et al. The development of the PROMPT criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484, Table 4
source.citation: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484
source.credit: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484

plain_summary: Clarithromycin and erythromycin slow the breakdown of carbamazepine, so its level can rise and cause headache, drowsiness and nausea.

medicine_groups.name: Carbamazepine
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, slow-release tablets and liquid count.

medicine_groups.name: Clarithromycin and erythromycin
medicine_groups.note: Azithromycin and roxithromycin are other macrolide antibiotics that the criterion does not name, so they do not count. Nexium Hp7 contains oral clarithromycin.

rule_for_models: For a patient aged 45 to 64 inclusive, start with the systemic clarithromycin (including Nexium Hp7) or systemic erythromycin line (if age is missing, record eligibility as unknown and report no finding). Calculate the antibiotic's last day first, counting for each supply from the labelled start date or else the supply date and adding the number of days given by the quantity and directions minus one. Look back from that last day and cite both lines with their date ranges when a carbamazepine supply had started by then and lasted at least until the antibiotic began, or cite both as a possible overlap only if timing is unclear and the supply dates are within 60 days of each other.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the patient actually took the antibiotic while taking carbamazepine, the carbamazepine blood level, and the reason for each medicine. Also any supply from another pharmacy or a hospital.
ask_the_gp: Could we review the combination today if both medicines are being taken or the antibiotic is about to start, including whether a different antibiotic or a carbamazepine level is appropriate? If the overlap has ended and there are no ongoing signs of toxicity, could we review it at the next routine medicines review?
